pages.text: The Platonic Realm is six layers, one for each part of mathematics, from Y −768 at the bottom to 1536 at the top. Between each layer and the next lies a wide gap of empty air, a hundred blocks and more: too far to climb, and too far to fall.

$(li)$(thing)The Infinite$() (Y 1280 to 1536): the Transfinite Hierarchy's strata, set theory.$(li)$(thing)The Continuum$() (islands at Y 880 to 1040): analysis.$(li)$(thing)Curved Space$() (Y 560 to 720): topology.$(li)$(thing)The Elements$() (Y 320 to 400): Euclid, the safe layer.$(li)$(thing)The Number Line$() (Y 10 to 194): the Realm's own islands.$(li)$(thing)The Axioms$() (Y −720 to −650): logic, far below the rest.

The $(item)Platonic Compass$() brings you to the Number Line. In the Realm, sneak and use it to climb one layer, or sneak, look down and use it to go down one; it lands you on the next layer's islands. It climbs no higher than the Continuum.

The widest gap of all, 240 blocks of nothing, lies under the $(thing)Infinite$(), and only the $(item)Cantor Key$() opens it: fly or climb up to it and you are turned back just below. From the Infinite, the Compass (sneaking, looking down) takes you back to the Continuum. Fall out of the bottom of the Axioms and you land in the Quantum Foam.

Each layer has its own stone, ore, landmarks, creature and music, and something it does to visitors (only ever an effect: nothing there changes a block). Each stone is also its field's raw feedstock, and each can be made again from cobblestone and a little of its layer's material, so building with it never runs out. Snow never settles here: the Realm is warm all the way up.
